items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: So Clarence Ford, we graduated from high school together... Oh yeah, yeah. That's when I came out of the service... the name of the band was Wallace Devin Bode and his bebop jockeys.

ctx.x: was playing. But all three of us had teachers. Did you have a band with Clarence Ford?

Oh yeah, yeah. That's when I came out of the service. We had also created by Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker. I called all the old musicians up whom I played with and told them I didn't want to play with them no more. That's because the music you're playing is old, that's out of style. I'm playing bebop now. So Clarence Ford, we graduated from high school together. From Booker T. Washington? Yeah, same class. And Wilbur Hogan too. Did you have him? Yeah. Wilbur Hogan? Yeah. We graduated together. And he, what…
You were talking about Clarence Ford and you know how?

items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: That's where the King Zulu used to go and drink his toast. Well, we would go there and see them.

ctx.x: I think still, people still do that today. I think I've been to a few parades. Yeah. People still do that. What'd you do, what'd you do as a kid on Mardi Gras Day? Was that a special day for you, for your family?

Yes and no. Well, before I would, before I started playing in the parades, and playing on the trucks, we'd stay in front of our house, either go to a jack, two blocks away from our home, where they had the funeral home. That's where the King Zulu used to go and drink his toast. Well, we would go there and see them. Then we would go to Canal, I mean to St. Charles and Frays, and see Rex. Then we'd come on back home, and just stay in front of our house. There wasn't too much going on out there. Because Mardi Gras…
Were you scared of the Indians as a child?
